question.text: Cash-equivalents (e.g., treasury bills, liquid funds) are PRIMARILY used for:

explanation.text: The Logic: Source p.13 says savers use short-term deposits or securities that are highly liquid; p.86 says liquid funds invest in short-term instruments for quick liquidity; and p.177 lists treasury bills among money-market instruments. Together these support cash-equivalents being primarily used for liquidity management and short-term parking. The Trap: Long-term growth is sought through equity; hedging and leverage are derivative-based uses, not the primary purpose of cash-equivalents. Note: Source p.126 frames the emergency cash reserve as usually two to three months of spending.
